''Zamia longifolia'' Jacqin | range_map = Encephalartos longifolius, verspreiding, a.png | range_map_caption = {{leftlegend|#FF0E17|range of species|outline=gray}} }} '''''Encephalartos longifolius''''' is a low-growing [[Arecaceae|palm]]-like [[cycad]] in the family [[Zamiaceae]]. It is endemic to [[South Africa]] and is commonly known as '''Thunberg's cycad''', '''breadpalm''' or '''broodboom'''.Palmer, E. and Pitman, N. ''Trees of southern Africa, covering all known indigenous species in the Republic of South Africa, South-West Africa, Botswana, Lesotho & Swaziland''. Cape Town (1972). This cycad is listed as near threatened in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. ==Description== [[file:Encephalartos_longifolius02.jpg|thumb|left|''E. longifolius'' growing at the [[Orto botanico di Palermo]]]] [[file:Encephalartos longifolius - Villa Thuret - DSC04828.JPG|thumb|left|The male cone]] The breadpalm grows up to three metres tall and develops a very thick trunk with age. This is crowned with dark or metallic green, semi-glossy, arching leaves up to two metres long and moderately keeled. The leaflets are lanceolate, overlapping upwards and have smooth margins. There are one to three green, ovoid male cones 40 to 60 centimetres long and 15 to 20 centimetres in diameter. This is the largest pollen cones in its genus.{{cite book | last= Giddy | first= Cynthia | date= 1974 | title= Cycads of South Africa | location= Cape Town| publisher= Purnell |page= 92 }} A similar number of green female cones are more robust with a diameter of up to forty centimetres. The seeds are red and can reach five centimetres long.{{Cite web|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/cycadpg?taxname=Encephalartos+longifolius|title=Encephalartos longifolius|website=plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au|access-date=2017-08-01|archive-date=2014-06-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140623210845/http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/cycadpg?taxname=Encephalartos+longifolius|url-status=dead}} ==Distribution== This species is found in coastal regions of [[Eastern Cape|Eastern Cape Province]], [[South Africa]] growing at heights of up to six hundred metres. It grows in a variety of different habitats on the mountain ridges from west of [[Joubertina]] in the [[Kouga Local Municipality|Kouga]] mountains east to near [[Grahamstown]]. There are a large number of locations where breadpalms grow but on the whole, populations are declining. ==Historical note== In their book on South African trees, published in 1972, [[Eve Palmer]] and Norah Pitman wrote: {{quote|This was the first cycad seen by the early colonists pushing eastwards. This was Thunberg's breadtree; and this species almost changed the course of South African history for its seeds nearly killed General [[Jan Smuts|Smuts]] and men of a Boer commando in the [[eastern Cape]] during the [[Second Boer War|Anglo-Boer War]]. Colonel [[Deneys Reitz]] writes in his book Commando how Smuts and his men, camping on the Suurberg, were poisoned after eating the seeds of ''[[Encephalartos altensteinii]]''. Botanists today know that Reitz mistook the species, and that it was Thunberg's breadtree that poisoned the party.}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{commonscat-inline|Encephalartos longifolius|''Encephalartos longifolius''}} * {{wikispecies-inline|Encephalartos longifolius|''Encephalartos longifolius''}} *[http://www.conifers.org/za/Encephalartos_lehmannii.php The Gymnosperm Database.] {{Taxonbar|from=Q3724985}} [[Category:Encephalartos|longifolius]] [[Category:Trees of South Africa]]
